what: Papua New Guinea faces severe food shortages as El Niño brings frost and drought

clean_source_blocks.text: Oxfam predicts PNG will be worst-hit country in Pacific from the weather pattern, with up to 3 million people affected nationwide Families across Papua New Guinea’s Highlands are facing depleted harvests and the threat of hunger after the El Niño weather pattern brought frost and prolonged dry conditions that have destroyed food gardens providing sustenance and income for thousands of households. The effects of El Niño emerged in recent weeks, bringing drought conditions, falling water levels and frost that are threatening food security in some of the country’s most agriculturally productive regions. Continue reading...

Oxfam predicts PNG will be worst-hit country in Pacific from the weather pattern, with up to 3 million people affected nationwide Families across Papua New Guinea’s Highlands are facing depleted harvests and the threat of hunger after the El Niño weather pattern brought frost and prolonged dry conditions that have destroyed food gardens providing sustenance and income for thousands of households. The effects of El Niño emerged in recent weeks, bringing drought conditions, falling water levels and frost that are threatening food security in some of the country’s most agriculturally productive regions. According to Oxfam PNG, Papua New Guinea is currently the Pacific’s worst-hit country from the impacts of El Niño. The aid agency said rainfall had been below average for almost a year and, combined with frost in the Highlands and invasive pests, had destroyed crops and livestock.

Oxfam PNG estimates that up to 3 million people could be affected nationwide, including a projected 1.9 million in the Highlands region. Communities that rely heavily on farming are already experiencing severe food shortages, with some reporting that food supplies may last only two to three months. The agency warned that households forced to reduce meals and eat less variety are at increased risk of malnutrition. Papua New Guinea’s National Weather Service says El Niño is causing severe drought and damaging frost by shifting rainfall away from the country and reducing moisture levels. The lack of cloud cover allows heat to escape rapidly at night, causing temperatures in the Highlands to drop below freezing and triggering frosts that can destroy crops.

Speaking at a news conference today, the Director for PNG National Weather Service Mr. Samuel Maiha said the country is in El-Nino now and is going to be affected very severely over the next four months. Maiha added that indicators confirm the adverse conditions will last well into March or April and possibly, even May of 2016. The tropical highlands of Papua New Guinea and the Solomon Islands are experiencing frosts and cold winds that have already devastated families food crops, killing everything from the islands’ staple, the sweet potato, to cabbage, lettuce and English potatoes, reports ABC.net.au. Mr. Maiha also pointed out that with little or no rainfall, far greater areas will become dry, with 85 percent of the population facing water shortages, a poor planting season and an increase in disease outbreaks.

original_article.research:
[Lähde: The Guardian World]
Oxfam predicts PNG will be worst-hit country in Pacific from the weather pattern, with up to 3 million people affected nationwide

Families across Papua New Guinea’s Highlands are facing depleted harvests and the threat of hunger after the El Niño weather pattern brought frost and prolonged dry conditions that have destroyed food gardens providing sustenance and income for thousands of households.

The effects of El Niño emerged in recent weeks, bringing drought conditions, falling water levels and frost that are threatening food security in some of the country’s most agriculturally productive regions.

According to Oxfam PNG, Papua New Guinea is currently the Pacific’s worst-hit country from the impacts of El Niño. The aid agency said rainfall had been below average for almost a year and, combined with frost in the Highlands and invasive pests, had destroyed crops and livestock.

Oxfam PNG estimates that up to 3 million people could be affected nationwide, including a projected 1.9 million in the Highlands region. Communities that rely heavily on farming are already experiencing severe food shortages, with some reporting that food supplies may last only two to three months.

The agency warned that households forced to reduce meals and eat less variety are at increased risk of malnutrition.

Papua New Guinea’s National Weather Service says El Niño is causing severe drought and damaging frost by shifting rainfall away from the country and reducing moisture levels. The lack of cloud cover allows heat to escape rapidly at night, causing temperatures in the Highlands to drop below freezing and triggering frosts that can destroy crops.

In Tambul, Western Highlands province, farmer John Wankar woke last week to find his food garden covered in frost, with vegetables and staple crops damaged. Wankar said his family relied entirely on the garden for food and income and now faced uncertainty about how they would survive in the coming weeks.

In Chimbu’s Kundiawa-Gembogl district, 62-year-old Martha John described a similar experience after frost swept through her community.

“Last week Wednesday, all our gardens were covered in frost,” she said.

“We wept, as these gardens are not only for us to eat but also our income. We have been growing potato and selling them in bulks, and all my children and grandchildren depend on this food for eating and also for income.”

[Lähde: Digital Journal]
Speaking at a news conference today, the Director for PNG National Weather Service Mr. Samuel Maiha said the country is in El-Nino now and is going to be affected very severely over the next four months.

Maiha added that indicators confirm the adverse conditions will last well into March or April and possibly, even May of 2016. The tropical highlands of Papua New Guinea and the Solomon Islands are experiencing frosts and cold winds that have already devastated families food crops, killing everything from the islands’ staple, the sweet potato, to cabbage, lettuce and English potatoes, reports ABC.net.au.

Mr. Maiha also pointed out that with little or no rainfall, far greater areas will become dry, with 85 percent of the population facing water shortages, a poor planting season and an increase in disease outbreaks.

The Enga province administrator, Samson Amean called a meeting with the PNG provincial disaster and emergency committee on Monday after finding out hundreds of families are now without any food crops for months to come.

Governor William Powi of the Southern Highlands province declared a state of emergency because of the disaster. Dr. Amean said many people in the highlands have already started moving to lower altitudes where they have relatives.

In the East New Britain province, water has become so scarce that people are getting water from the Warongoi River, a water source possibly contaminated by a cyanide spill at the nearby Sinivit mining site. Officials confirm many dead fish have been seen, and a number of people have fallen ill after eating them. The spill occurred many months ago, and provincial leaders are still waiting for test results.

PNG government promises aid
The PNG government is promising immediate disaster funds for the affected population. At the same time, they are defending their decision on a ban of limited agricultural produce imports. All this is going on as the country battles the effects of El Nino and a severe lack of infrastructure.

Some have criticised the ban, saying transportation and storage infrastructure has left farmers unprepared for the increased demand. But now, with the country in dire straits because of El Nino, the ban is laughable. NG Minister for Agriculture and Livestock Tommy Tomscoll dismissed critics, and actually downplayed the severe drought.

payload.title: El Niño uhkaa Papua-Uuden-Guinean ruokaturvaa
payload.summary: Papua-Uuden-Guinean ylängöillä pakkanen ja pitkään jatkunut kuivuus ovat tuhonneet kotitalouksien ruokapuutarhoja. Oxfamin arvion mukaan jopa kolme miljoonaa ihmistä voi kärsiä El Niñon vaikutuksista eri puolilla maata.
payload.content:
Papua-Uudessa-Guineassa pelätään vakavaa ruokapulaa, kun El Niño -sääilmiö on tuonut maan ylänköalueille kuivuutta, vedenpintojen laskua ja hallaa. Avustusjärjestö Oxfam arvioi, että vaikutukset voivat koskea valtakunnallisesti jopa kolmea miljoonaa ihmistä, joista noin 1,9 miljoonaa asuu ylänköseudulla.

## Sadot ovat ehtyneet ylängöillä

Erityisen vaikea tilanne on Papua-Uuden-Guinean Highlands-alueella, jossa monet perheet ovat riippuvaisia pienviljelystä sekä ruoan että tulojen lähteenä. El Niñon vaikutukset ovat viime viikkoina näkyneet pitkittyneinä kuivina jaksoina, vedenpintojen laskuna ja hallana, jotka ovat tuhonneet ruokapuutarhoja ja heikentäneet kotitalouksien mahdollisuuksia selviytyä omavaraisesti.

Oxfam PNG:n mukaan Papua-Uusi-Guinea on tällä hetkellä Tyynenmeren alueen pahimmin El Niñosta kärsivä maa. Järjestö kertoo sateiden jääneen keskimääräistä vähäisemmiksi lähes vuoden ajan. Kuivuuden lisäksi ylänköjen hallat ja haitalliset vieraslajit ovat vahingoittaneet sekä satoja että karjaa.

## Ruokavarastot voivat loppua nopeasti

Maataloudesta riippuvaiset yhteisöt kärsivät jo vakavasta ruokapulasta. Joissakin yhteisöissä on raportoitu, että jäljellä olevat ruokavarastot voivat riittää vain kahdesta kolmeen kuukauteen. Oxfam varoittaa, että kotitaloudet joutuvat vähentämään aterioita ja syömään yksipuolisemmin, mikä lisää aliravitsemuksen riskiä.

Papua-Uuden-Guinean kansallisen sääpalvelun mukaan El Niño aiheuttaa vakavaa kuivuutta ja vahingollisia halloja siirtämällä sateita pois maan yltä ja vähentämällä ilmankosteutta. Kun pilvipeite ohenee, lämpöä karkaa öisin nopeasti, ja ylänköalueiden lämpötila voi laskea pakkasen puolelle.

Hallat voivat tuhota viljelykasveja nopeasti alueilla, jotka kuuluvat maan tärkeimpiin maataloustuotannon seutuihin. Aiemmissa vastaavissa oloissa ylängöillä on raportoitu vahinkoja muun muassa bataatille, kaalille, salaatille ja perunalle. Sääpalvelun johtaja Samuel Maiha on kuvannut El Niñon voivan tuoda vakavia vaikutuksia useiden kuukausien ajaksi, ja vähäinen sade lisää myös huolta vesipulasta, heikosta istutuskaudesta ja tautiriskien kasvusta.
summary_bullets: Oxfam arvioi, että El Niñon vaikutukset voivat koskea Papua-Uudessa-Guineassa jopa kolmea miljoonaa ihmistä.
Ylänköalueilla kuivuus, vedenpintojen lasku ja halla ovat tuhonneet ruokapuutarhoja ja heikentäneet satoja.
Kotitalouksien aterioiden vähentäminen ja yksipuolistuva ruokavalio lisäävät aliravitsemuksen riskiä.
payload.journalist_note: Korjattu artikkeli laajentaa lähdepaketin Oxfamin ja Papua-Uuden-Guinean sääpalvelun tietoihin sekä erottaa vanhemmasta taustalohkosta vain yleisesti soveltuvat, lähteessä mainitut vaikutusmekanismit ja satovahinkoesimerkit.
